page.layout: One column of text, centred to the right of the page. No margin notes. Running head with page number at the top. Lines of Latin and German (black letter) run down the column, with rules and headings between them. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Quinta actio introducta est de peculio, deque eo, quod in rem domini versum erit. §. praeterea. institut. eod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST OCTAVUS Titulus? De noxalibus actionibus. Von flagen[?] erlittener beschädi-ung halben.

p.i: Quid proditum est ex maleficiis servorum?

main_text.p: EX maleficiis servorum: veluti si furtum fecerint; aut bona rapuerint, aut damnum dederint, aut injuriam commiserint: noxales actiones proditae sunt, quibus domino damnato permittitur, aut litis aestimationem sufferre, aut ipsum hominem noxae dedere, den menschen selbs für den schaden zur straff heimgeben. in princ. inst. eod.
Noxa est ipsum corpus quod nocuit: id est, servus: Noxia ipsum maleficium, veluti furtum, damnum, rapina, injuria. §. noxa autem. inst. eo.

Omnis noxalis actio caput sequitur. Nam si servus tuus noxam commiserit: quamdiu in tua potestate sit, tecum est Actio: si autem in alterius potestatem pervenerit: cum illo incipit actio esse. §. omnis autem. inst. eod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST NONUS Titulus? Si quadrupes pauperiem fecisse dicatur, So ein vierfüssiges thier schaden gethan hat.

page.notes: The German black-letter passages are marked with bl. The word "flagen" in the first German heading line is doubtful and is marked [?]; the first letter may be a K in black letter. A stain covers the top right corner. Line ends are hyphenated as printed ("er-", "beschädi-", "insti-"). The catchword "Qui" sits at the bottom right, partly cut off by the edge of the scan.
